title: Best Smartphones UK
short: Seven smartphones lab-tested for performance, display, battery life and camera quality, from a £153 budget Motorola to a £1,549 Samsung foldable.
intro: Choosing a phone from marketing photos and spec sheets alone can be misleading, since real-world battery life and camera performance often differ from the numbers on the box. This guide is based on Expert Reviews' tested roundup (updated 29 June 2026), where testers benchmark CPU and GPU performance with Geekbench 5 and GFXBench, measure display brightness, contrast and colour accuracy with DisplayCAL software and a colorimeter, run an in-house battery rundown test (looping video in flight mode at 170cd/m² brightness until the phone shuts down), and test cameras across scenic, low-light, indoor and rapid-panning video scenarios. Expert Reviews has tested over 600 phones using this process.

products.name: Galaxy S25 Ultra
products.best_for: Buyers who want the fastest all-round flagship with the strongest zoom
products.key_spec: 6.9" AMOLED, Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, quad camera (200MP/50MP/10MP/50MP), 100x zoom, Android 15
products.summary: Expert Reviews recorded exceptional performance and the fastest CPU scores of any phone tested, paired with exceptional battery longevity for a flagship. The 100x telephoto zoom impressed testers with greater detail retention and less over-sharpening than rivals, though screen brightness trails some competitors and the price is a lot to swallow.
pros: Fastest CPU scores recorded in testing

products.name: Moto G56
products.best_for: Buyers who want maximum durability and a bright screen for the least money
products.key_spec: 6.72" LCD, Dimensity 7060, dual camera (50MP/8MP), IP68/IP69 rated, Gorilla Glass 7i
products.summary: Expert Reviews found exceptional durability for a budget phone, with water and dust resistance that actually exceeds some flagships. The large display hit a bright 861cd/m² peak in testing, though gaming performance is limited and it's only promised two years of OS updates, a genuine downside at this end of the market.
pros: Exceptional durability for the price, beats some flagships
cons: Only two years of OS updates promised

products.name: iPhone 17 Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who want the best balance of iPhone power and price
products.key_spec: 6.3" OLED, Apple A19 Pro, triple 48MP cameras, iOS 26
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this the 'sweet spot' in Apple's current line-up, combining strong power with more reasonable pricing than the top model. Battery life exceeded 31 hours in testing, and the all-48MP camera array delivered crisp, impeccably lit shots with beautiful dynamic range, though the design was seen as a step down and the 4x telephoto lags rivals.
pros: Strong battery life in testing (31+ hours)
Better value than Apple's top-tier model

products.best_for: Buyers who hate charging their phone and want it to just keep going
products.key_spec: 6.78" AMOLED, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, 7,300mAh battery, Android 16
products.summary: Expert Reviews recorded a record-breaking 45+ hour battery endurance in testing, beating the next-best phone by a full seven hours. Display brightness and colour accuracy both impressed, and it can shoot Dolby Vision 4K at 120fps, though only four OS updates are promised and testers found AI zoom overbearing beyond 30x magnification.
pros: Excellent display brightness and colour accuracy
cons: AI zoom quality drops off past 30x

products.name: Find X9 Pro
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise photography above everything else
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this a 'phenomenal camera suite', with an exceptional 200MP telephoto delivering detailed 3x and 6x optical/hybrid zooms, and all four 50MP-class sensors performing excellently. Oversharpening crept in past 60x zoom, 8K video is missing, and testers found the camera button placement fiddly, but overall image quality led the group.

products.name: Pixel 9a
products.best_for: Buyers who want flagship-length software support at a mid-range price
products.key_spec: 6.3" OLED, Google Tensor G4, dual camera (48MP/13MP), seven years of software support
products.summary: Expert Reviews highlighted flagship-level seven-year software support as a genuine standout for the price, alongside battery life that exceeded 34 hours in testing. The display measured a gorgeous Delta E of 0.67 for colour accuracy, though there's no telephoto lens and the design was criticised as generic.
pros: Seven years of promised software support
Strong battery life in testing (34+ hours)

products.name: Galaxy Z Fold 7
products.best_for: Buyers who want a tablet-sized screen that folds down to phone size
products.key_spec: 8" internal / 6.5" cover AMOLED, Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, 200MP main camera, 4.2mm folded thickness
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this incredibly slim and lightweight for a foldable, with the fastest foldable performance the publication has recorded. The 200MP main camera captured crisp, colourful images in testing, though S Pen support has been removed and dust protection is limited to particles over 1mm.
pros: Incredibly slim and lightweight for a foldable
cons: Dust protection limited to larger particles

guide.a: Expert Reviews rated the iPhone 17 Pro as the best iPhone, praising its camera array and battery life, while flagship Android options like the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra and Oppo Find X9 Pro edged ahead on raw performance and zoom capability. The choice often comes down to which ecosystem, iOS or Android, you're already invested in through apps and accessories.

guide.q: Do I need a flagship, or is mid-range enough?
guide.a: Expert Reviews found the Google Pixel 9a delivers flagship-level software support (seven years) and strong battery life for under half the price of the top phones here. Unless you specifically want the fastest chipset or the best zoom camera, a well-chosen mid-range phone like this covers most everyday needs.

guide.q: How much does battery life actually vary?
guide.a: Quite a lot in Expert Reviews' testing: the OnePlus 15 ran for over 45 hours in their video rundown test, seven hours longer than the next best phone, while other flagships managed around 31-34 hours. If battery anxiety is a priority, check a phone's tested runtime rather than just its mAh rating, since efficiency varies by chipset.

guide.q: Is a foldable phone worth the extra cost and compromises?
guide.a: Expert Reviews found the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 7 genuinely impressive for its slimness and performance, offering a tablet-sized screen that folds to phone size. It costs significantly more than a standard flagship and comes with trade-offs like reduced dust protection, so it suits buyers who specifically want the larger unfolded screen for work or media.
